answer: I'd like to talk about a jacket that I probably wear more than anything else I own. A piece of clothing I am particularly fond of is a simple, well-made jacket I bought a few years ago. It's a plain navy one with a soft lining and a couple of deep inside pockets. It is nothing flashy, but it has become a real [[staple]] of my wardrobe. I wear it mostly in winter, because the mornings in the north of Bangladesh can get surprisingly chilly, and it's perfect for my early walks by the river. What I love about it is how [[versatile]] it is; I can wear it to work, to a casual outing or even a semi-formal event. I bought it in Dhaka while I was visiting my elder sister, and she helped me choose it after I'd spent ages hesitating between two colours, so it also carries a nice memory. It fits me perfectly and is remarkably comfortable, which matters far more to me than following trends. Despite years of regular use, it has proved incredibly [[durable]] and still looks good. Honestly, I have come to appreciate quality over quantity when it comes to clothes. A single well-chosen item like this is worth more than a dozen cheap ones. It has become something of a [[signature piece]] for me, and I always feel [[confident]] wearing it. I suspect I will keep wearing it until it finally falls apart.

followUps.q: Do you usually wear traditional or Western clothes?
followUps.answer: Mostly Western clothes for work, like shirts and trousers. But for Eid, weddings and Friday prayers I prefer a panjabi, which feels more comfortable and more [[in keeping with]] the occasion.

followUps.q: Do you enjoy shopping for clothes?
followUps.answer: Not particularly, to be honest. I tend to put it off until I really need something, and I'd rather buy one good item than spend hours browsing through shops full of things I don't need.

note: Persona fix: bought in Dhaka with his elder sister instead of 'during a trip abroad'; added description and when he wears it (northern winter mornings); new mark 'signature piece'.
